## Enterprise software design and evolution

Integration, modernization and technical decisions for software that supports business operations.

### Areas of work

**Technical design.** Responsibilities, dependencies and implementation options for changes to an enterprise system.

**Enterprise integration.** Processes connecting applications and data, with attention to information integrity and recovery from failures.

**System evolution.** Incremental modernization of existing software, considering testing, delivery and operational continuity.

### Explore the work

[Background, areas of work and writing](https://johndgomez.com/) · [John D. Gómez’s individual profile](https://github.com/johndgomezh)

<details>
<summary>Terms and notation</summary>

An **integration** enables different systems to exchange information and take part in a process. **Incremental modernization** introduces changes to an existing system in stages. **Operational continuity** is the ability to maintain or recover necessary business activities through changes or disruptions. **GitHub** is the platform hosting this organization and supporting collaboration on software repositories. The middle dot **·** separates related links. In an email address, **@** separates the mailbox from the domain. The initial **D.** belongs to the public name John D. Gómez.


**Reading the file.** This document uses **Markdown**, a text format: `##` and `###` introduce different heading levels; `**text**` adds emphasis; a leading hyphen introduces a list item. `[text](destination)` creates a link; `https://` begins a web address and `mailto:` prepares an email. Backticks mark literal names or instructions. Two spaces at the end of a line create a line break.

**Images and paths.** HTML tags are enclosed in `<` and `>`; a slash before a tag name closes its element. `picture` groups image variants; `source` selects a variant; `media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"` activates the variant when the device requests a dark theme; `srcset` and `src` identify image files; `img` displays the image; `alt` provides an accessible name and `width="520"` sets a reference width of 520 pixels. The `=` sign assigns an attribute value and quotes enclose that value. `details` creates this expandable section and `summary` controls it. In paths, `/` separates folders and `..` means the parent folder. `assets/wordmark` stores the graphic name; `on-dark.svg` and `on-light.svg` are its variants for dark and light backgrounds. SVG is a vector image format; `.md` identifies Markdown; `README` names the introductory file; `.en` indicates English and `translations` holds the translation. The initial **D.** belongs to the public name John D. Gómez.

</details>
